items.title: Scientists warn mega-constellations could devastate ozone layer

featured_image.name: Satellite Mega Constellations Could Jeopardize Ozone-Hole ...

items.description: The race to fill low Earth orbit with vast fleets of satellites is raising alarms among atmospheric scientists, who warn that the mass burning of defunct spacecraft could damage the ozone layer and alter Earth's climate in ways that remain poorly understood. With SpaceX seeking permission to launch up to one million satellites and more than 1.23 million spacecraft now proposed worldwide, researchers and policymakers are calling for global regulation before the atmospheric consequences become irreversible.[1][2]

items.description: Oil prices swung sharply on Thursday, initially tumbling before reversing course, as traders weighed a massive buildup in U.S. crude inventories against signs that nuclear talks between Washington and Tehran were hitting a wall. The volatile session underscored the competing forces gripping global energy markets: ample domestic supply on one side, and the threat of military conflict in the Middle East on the other.

items.title: Zelenskiy says next Ukraine-Russia talks to move to Abu Dhabi in early March

featured_image.name: First day of trilateral talks on Russia-Ukraine war ends in Abu Dhabi

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy announced on Thursday that the next round of U.S.-brokered trilateral peace negotiations between Ukraine and Russia will likely take place in Abu Dhabi in early March, according to Reuters. The announcement came during Zelenskiy's evening address, following a day of preparatory bilateral talks in Geneva between Ukrainian and American officials focused on post-war reconstruction.[1][2]

The Geneva meeting — led by Ukraine's chief negotiator Rustem Umerov and U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff alongside presidential adviser Jared Kushner — centered on a proposed "prosperity package" designed to mobilize public and private investment for Ukraine's economic recovery. Kyiv aims to attract roughly $800 billion over the next decade to rebuild the country, according to Reuters, while the World Bank's latest assessment estimates reconstruction costs at approximately $588 billion.[3][4][5]

items.title: US, Iran to hold Vienna nuclear talks next week

featured_image.name: U.S. and Iran say progress made in Geneva nuclear talks

items.description:
The United States and Iran will hold technical-level nuclear discussions next week in Vienna after concluding a third round of indirect negotiations in Geneva on Thursday, Oman's foreign minister announced.

"We have finished the day after significant progress in the negotiation between the United States and Iran," Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi wrote on X. "We will resume soon after consultation in the respective capitals. Discussions on a technical level will take place next week in Vienna."[1][2]

The choice of Vienna, home to the International Atomic Energy Agency, underscores the increasingly technical nature of the negotiations over Tehran's nuclear program. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi was present during Thursday's session, according to Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei.[3][4]

items.title: Afghanistan launches border offensive against Pakistan

featured_image.name: Pakistan claims to have killed at least 70 militants in strikes along Afghan border

items.description: Afghanistan's Taliban forces launched what they described as large-scale offensive operations against Pakistani military positions along the Durand Line late Thursday, retaliating for Pakistani airstrikes earlier in the week that Kabul says killed civilians. Pakistan said it responded to what it called "unprovoked fire" across multiple sectors in its northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, with both sides claiming to have inflicted heavy casualties on the other. The exchange threatens to unravel a fragile ceasefire that had been in place since October 2025.

items.title: Pentagon's kamikaze drone unit ready for Iran strikes

featured_image.name: Pentagon's Kamikaze Drone Unit Ready for Possible Iran ...

items.description:
The Pentagon's first one-way attack drone unit, Task Force Scorpion Strike, is operationally prepared to participate in potential strikes against Iran if President Donald Trump orders military action, according to Bloomberg, citing U.S. officials and analysts. The unit's readiness adds a new capability to an already massive American military buildup in the Middle East, where two aircraft carrier strike groups, stealth fighters, and long-range bombers are now positioned within striking range of Iran.[1][2]

The development comes as the United States and Iran held a third round of indirect nuclear negotiations in Geneva on Thursday, with the two sides exchanging proposals through Omani mediators amid deepening uncertainty over whether diplomacy can avert a military confrontation.[3][4]

items.title: US, Iran show 'unprecedented openness' in Geneva nuclear talks

featured_image.name: US, Iran Resume Nuclear Talks as Trump's Deal Deadline ...

items.description:
Iran and the United States held a third round of indirect nuclear negotiations in Geneva on Thursday, with Oman mediating the high-stakes talks as President Donald Trump's deadline for a deal rapidly approaches. The discussions, which adjourned for a midday break before resuming, were described by Iranian officials as having progressed "very intensely and very seriously," according to Bloomberg.[1]

Oman's Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, who has been shuttling between the two delegations at his country's embassy in Geneva, said the Iranian and American teams showed "unprecedented openness to new and creative ideas and solutions". The U.S. delegation is led by Trump's special Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff and his son-in-law Jared Kushner, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi heads Tehran's team.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Google rolls out Nano Banana 2 as default AI image model across Gemini

featured_image.name: Google launches Nano Banana Pro powered by Gemini 3 - CNBC

items.description:
Google on Thursday unveiled Nano Banana 2, the latest version of its viral AI image generation tool, rolling it out as the default image model across the Gemini app, Google Search, and its video editing tool Flow. Officially designated Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, the upgrade brings capabilities previously reserved for the higher-end Nano Banana Pro model to a broader audience at faster speeds.[1][2]

The new model produces images with resolutions ranging from 512 pixels to 4K across multiple aspect ratios, supports character consistency for up to five characters, and can maintain fidelity of up to 14 objects in a single workflow, according to TechCrunch. It also inherits Nano Banana Pro's advanced world knowledge, accurate text rendering, and the ability to generate data visualizations and infographics — features that made the Pro version popular among creators and professionals.[3][2][1]
